_comment: The opt-out route (design D16) and the audit record every do-not-contact or consent change writes (design D17). Written 2026-11-05 from Platform main a1fc0481 by reading the code, folding the judge's ruling on Q2 (the route) and Q5; nothing here was run and the route does not exist today. POST /api/v1/contacts/{id}/opt-out ONLY RESTRICTS: it can set `doNotContact` to true and record `false` for the channels it names; it never clears do-not-contact and never records `true` (the permissive direction stays on PUT /contacts/{id} behind contacts:contact:edit, design D3). Permission: contacts:conversation:handle (the agent, supervisor, manager templates and the admin family hold it; quality_analyst and api do not), evaluated first in the handler through IAuthorizationService with `Permission:contacts:conversation:handle` (design D2's mechanism; PermissionPolicyProvider.cs:8, 18-20 resolves any `Permission:` policy), refused with the ErrorResponse of contact-write-refusals.v1.json. Evaluation order: 1. permission -> 403 not-permitted; 2. `channels` validated as `channelConsent` keys are on PUT (ChannelType names compared ordinally) -> 400 unknown-consent-channel with `details`; 3. no contact of the tenant has that id -> 404, no body; 4. the write. A body that changes nothing (no `doNotContact: true`, no channel, or every named value already in place) answers 200 with the contact and writes nothing, audit included. The route wraps a service, IContactOptOutService, so an inbound processor can later call it with the actor `system`. ApiJsonContext: camelCase, enums as PascalCase strings, null members absent. Every child change's delta spec must cite these field names and codes VERBATIM.

request.case: an agent hears 'do not call me again, and no more SMS' and records it from the contact card

requestFields.doNotContact: boolean, optional: `true` sets the contact's do-not-contact; absent or `false` leaves it as stored (the route never clears it)
requestFields.channels: array of strings, optional: each a ChannelType name exactly as GET writes it (case-sensitive), recorded as `false` in `channelConsent`; channels not named keep their value

response._note: the Contact read model, the same shape PUT /contacts/{id} answers; the stored `channelConsent` was { "Voice": true } before the call. `updatedBy` is now written (the audit `actorId` of `audit.actorResolution`: here the agent's user id) by the opt-out and by PUT (design D17); today PUT writes only `updatedAt`

refusals.case: a caller whose roles hold no contacts:conversation:handle, e.g. the quality_analyst or api template, or a read-only impersonation token
a channel that is not a ChannelType name as GET writes it; nothing is written, `doNotContact` included
an id no contact of the tenant has

audit._comment: Not a wire shape the console consumes: the record IAuditService.RecordAsync writes (actor per `actorResolution`, never DncListEndpoints.cs:120's `sub ?? system`), read back through the existing audit log. Written when the route, PUT /contacts/{id} (only when `doNotContact` or a `channelConsent` key changes value) or DELETE /contacts/{id} changes something; never on a refusal or a no-op. `changes.before`/`after` hold ONLY `doNotContact` and `channelConsent`, never names or addresses. They are given as a typed sealed record registered in a source-generated JSON context the audit store serializes with (PostgresAuditStore.SerializeChange, :379-402; an unregistered type falls back to ToString() in the AOT image), or as pre-serialized JSON. `retainUntil` is the write time plus five years (IAuditService.cs:14-19, 32).

optOut._actor: a JWT agent: `actorId` its user id, `actorType` `user` (see `actorResolution`)

actorResolution._comment: design D17, second spec audit F1; read on Platform a1fc0481. actorId is CallerIdentity.ResolveUserId (CallerIdentity.cs:31-34, order user_id ?? NameIdentifier ?? sub); actorType `api_key` is the value AuditEntry.ActorType documents (AuditEntry.cs:43). Contact.UpdatedBy is set to the same actorId. Applies to contact.opted_out, contact.consent_changed and contact.deleted alike.

apiKeyBoundToUser.claims: NameIdentifier = key id, user_id = owner (ApiKeyAuthenticationHandler.cs:56, :94); no sub

apiKeyUnbound.claims: NameIdentifier = key id, no user_id, no sub; only a management key passes the permission (design D7)

service.claims: none: IContactOptOutService called with no HTTP caller (a later inbound processor)

update._changes: before/after of `doNotContact` and `channelConsent` only, as for `contact.opted_out`; `retainUntil` write time plus five years

delete._note: no `changes` and no addresses; `metadata.doNotContact` is the deleted contact's flag as a string. Optional (design D17): first to drop if the change must shrink
